tokyo_onigiri_asakusa_yadoroku.price_note: PARTIAL: the shop publishes its lunch sets with from-prices and does NOT publish its fillings list or the price of individual onigiri. It states 320円以上のおにぎりは差額分で承ります — onigiri above ¥320 are charged at the difference — which establishes ¥320 as the base but names no filling, so nothing is recorded about what they are. Tabelog not consulted: it has served Cf-Mitigated: challenge (HTTP 403) to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ AN ONIGIRI SPECIALIST IS ONE OF THE BEST FORMATS IN JAPAN FOR A COELIAC AND THIS IS THE OLDEST ONE IN TOKYO, opened 昭和29年 (1954). The construction is rice, nori and a filling: no batter, no noodle, no wrapper, no fryer, no roux. The shop names its own components — 大釜で炊かれたコシヒカリ, Koshihikari rice cooked in a large cauldron, wrapped in 江戸前の海苔, Edo-mae nori — and rice and seaweed are both clean. ⚠ SO THE WHOLE QUESTION IS THE FILLING, AND IT IS NOT PUBLISHED. The standard Japanese onigiri fillings divide sharply: 梅 (pickled plum) and 塩 are clean and plant; 昆布 is kelp simmered in SOY; おかか is bonito flakes with SOY, so fish and wheat; 鮭 and 明太子 and ツナマヨ are fish, the last with egg. A coeliac or vegan here has a real meal available and has to ask filling by filling — which at a counter that hands-forms one at a time, as this shop says it does (1個から握ります), is a conversation the format actually allows. ⚠ AND THE SET HAS TWO OTHER COMPONENTS: both lunch sets come with 豆腐味噌汁 and 沢庵. The miso soup is built on a DASHI, so it is fish and the miso may be barley; the takuan is pickled daikon, plant, though commercial takuan is often steeped in a soy-bearing liquid. 台東区浅草3-9-10, behind the Sensoji main hall; 11:30 and 17:00 seatings, closing when the rice runs out; closed Sundays at lunch and Sunday, Tuesday and Wednesday evenings; 8 counter seats and 8 at tables. Takeaway available and the shop delivers across Asakusa for large orders.

items.note: ⚠ THE RICE AND NORI ARE CLEAN; THE SET AROUND THEM IS NOT. A from-price, because the filling chosen changes it — the shop charges the difference on anything above ¥320. The MISO SOUP is the reason both flags are against rather than open: a Japanese miso soup is built on bonito DASHI, which makes the set fish, and miso koji is sometimes barley. Ask whether the soup can be left off or made without dashi, and the rest of this plate becomes one of the better prospects in Asakusa.
